evals.name: phys-opt-log-review
evals.prompt: I ran phys_opt_design with AggressiveExplore. Can you check the log and tell me if it was effective? How much did WNS/TNS improve?
evals.expected_output: Agent scopes log to phys_opt_design section via sed, extracts timing summaries [Physopt 32-668/603/619], per-phase optimization counts, and recommends next steps.

assertions.name: log_scoped_correctly
assertions.description: Log extraction was scoped to phys_opt_design section only
assertions.check: Agent used sed -n '/Command: phys_opt_design/,/phys_opt_design.*Time/p' or equivalent scoping, not a raw unscoped grep

assertions.name: timing_trend_extracted
assertions.description: WNS/TNS values from before and after phys_opt were reported
assertions.check: Output includes WNS/TNS values showing the trend across iterations (before vs after)

assertions.name: optimization_counts
assertions.description: Per-category optimization counts were extracted
assertions.check: Output includes counts for replication, retiming, rewiring, or other phys_opt categories

assertions.name: session_id_passed
assertions.description: session_id was passed to all vivado_execute calls
assertions.check: Every vivado_execute call includes session_id

evals.name: hold-fix-analysis
evals.prompt: phys_opt_design inserted a lot of LUT1 buffers for hold fixing. Is that normal? Can you analyze the hold-fix impact on setup timing?
evals.expected_output: Agent extracts [Physopt 32-234] hold fix results and [Physopt 32-960] skip messages, counts LUT1 insertions, assesses setup degradation, and recommends whether to adjust hold margin.

assertions.name: log_scoped_correctly
assertions.description: Log extraction was scoped to phys_opt_design section
assertions.check: Agent used sed scoping to extract only phys_opt_design section from log

assertions.name: hold_fix_counted
assertions.description: Hold-fix LUT1/ZHOLD_DELAY count was reported
assertions.check: Output includes count of hold-fix insertions from [Physopt 32-234] or LUT1 cell query

assertions.name: setup_impact_assessed
assertions.description: Impact of hold fix on setup timing was assessed
assertions.check: Output discusses whether hold-fix LUT1 insertions degraded setup WNS

evals.name: retiming-analysis
evals.prompt: I expected phys_opt_design retiming to help my critical paths but WNS barely changed. Can you check what happened with retiming?
evals.expected_output: Agent extracts retiming-specific messages [Physopt 32-942/943/952/953/847/735], reports candidate counts vs improvements, identifies why retiming was ineffective.

assertions.name: retiming_messages_checked
assertions.description: Retiming-specific message IDs were extracted from log
assertions.check: Output references [Physopt 32-942], [Physopt 32-952], [Physopt 32-953], or retiming candidate/improvement counts

assertions.name: blocking_reason_identified
assertions.description: Reason for ineffective retiming was identified
assertions.check: Output explains why retiming did not help (e.g., no candidates, DONT_TOUCH, improvement not found, async reset blocking)

assertions.name: log_scoped_correctly
assertions.description: Log extraction was scoped to phys_opt_design section
assertions.check: Agent used sed scoping, not unscoped grep

evals.name: uram-register-opt
evals.prompt: I have URAM-heavy paths that are timing critical. Did phys_opt_design push registers into the URAMs? Are there any candidates it missed?
evals.expected_output: Agent checks [Physopt 32-846] for no-candidate messages and any successful URAM register optimization, reports how many URAMs were optimized vs skipped.

assertions.name: uram_messages_checked
assertions.description: URAM register optimization messages were extracted
assertions.check: Output references [Physopt 32-846] (no candidates) or URAM register optimization results

assertions.name: recommendation_given
assertions.description: Recommendation was given for URAM register patterns
assertions.check: Output includes guidance on URAM-adjacent register patterns, enable/reset requirements, or -uram_register_opt option

evals.name: equivalent-driver-rewiring
evals.prompt: Can you check if equivalent driver rewiring helped during phys_opt_design? I have some nets with redundant drivers.
evals.expected_output: Agent extracts [Physopt 32-670/1030/1032/1487-1489] messages, reports candidate counts and optimization results, explains skip reasons.

assertions.name: eq_driver_messages_checked
assertions.description: Equivalent driver rewiring messages were extracted
assertions.check: Output references [Physopt 32-670] (skipped), [Physopt 32-1030] (candidates), [Physopt 32-1032] (result), or [Physopt 32-1488] (optimized group)

assertions.name: skip_reason_reported
assertions.description: If rewiring was skipped, the reason was reported
assertions.check: Output explains why equivalent driver rewiring was skipped (e.g., no setup violation, no equivalent drivers found)

evals.name: memory-rewire-opt
evals.prompt: phys_opt_design shows memory rewire optimization in the log. How effective was it? Did it improve timing on my BRAM paths?
evals.expected_output: Agent extracts [Physopt 32-1395/1396/1397/1398] MemoryRewireOpt messages, reports iteration-level pin rewire counts and WNS changes.

assertions.name: memory_rewire_messages
assertions.description: MemoryRewireOpt messages were extracted from log
assertions.check: Output references [Physopt 32-1395] (success), [Physopt 32-1396] (iteration detail), [Physopt 32-1398] (pins rewired), or [Physopt 32-1397] (failed)

assertions.name: timing_impact_reported
assertions.description: Timing impact of memory rewire was reported
assertions.check: Output includes WNS change or timing improvement data from memory rewire iterations

evals.name: dsp-bram-register-opt
evals.prompt: My DSP and BRAM paths are failing timing. Did phys_opt_design push registers into the hard macros?
evals.expected_output: Agent extracts DSP register [Physopt 32-456/457/665/666] and BRAM register [Physopt 32-526/527] messages, reports which macros had registers pushed in/out.

assertions.name: dsp_bram_messages_checked
assertions.description: DSP and BRAM register optimization messages were extracted
assertions.check: Output references DSP register messages ([Physopt 32-456/457/665/666]) and/or BRAM register messages ([Physopt 32-526/527])

assertions.name: candidates_vs_results
assertions.description: Candidate count vs optimization count was reported
assertions.check: Output distinguishes between candidates found and actual optimizations performed for DSP/BRAM registers

evals.name: fanout-replication-analysis
evals.prompt: phys_opt_design should have replicated some high-fanout net drivers. Can you tell me which nets were replicated and which were skipped?
evals.expected_output: Agent extracts [Physopt 32-76/65/569/571/232] messages, reports replicated vs skipped nets and reasons.

assertions.name: replication_messages_checked
assertions.description: Replication messages were extracted from log
assertions.check: Output references [Physopt 32-569] (replicated), [Physopt 32-571] (not replicated), [Physopt 32-76] (candidates), or [Physopt 32-65] (no nets found)

assertions.name: skip_reasons_reported
assertions.description: Reasons for skipped replication were reported
assertions.check: Output explains why specific nets were not replicated (e.g., fanout threshold, DONT_TOUCH, IS_REPLICABLE=FALSE)

evals.name: blocking-properties-inventory
evals.prompt: phys_opt_design seems to be skipping a lot of optimizations. I suspect DONT_TOUCH or MARK_DEBUG is blocking it. Can you check?
evals.expected_output: Agent queries design for PHYS_OPT_SKIPPED, DONT_TOUCH, IS_REPLICABLE=FALSE, and MARK_DEBUG properties, reports counts and affected timing paths.

assertions.name: blocking_props_queried
assertions.description: Blocking properties were queried via Vivado Tcl
assertions.check: Agent queried DONT_TOUCH, IS_REPLICABLE, MARK_DEBUG, or PHYS_OPT_SKIPPED properties via get_cells/get_nets

assertions.name: counts_reported
assertions.description: Counts of blocking properties were reported
assertions.check: Output includes counts for DONT_TOUCH cells, MARK_DEBUG nets, non-replicable primitives, or PHYS_OPT_SKIPPED cells

assertions.name: recommendation_given
assertions.description: Recommendation to resolve blocking was given
assertions.check: Output recommends removing DONT_TOUCH/MARK_DEBUG from timing-critical paths or using -force_replication_on_nets

evals.name: directive-recommendation
evals.prompt: I've run phys_opt_design twice with Default directive and WNS isn't improving much. What directive should I try next?
evals.expected_output: Agent analyzes the diminishing returns pattern, checks which optimizations were attempted, and recommends a specific directive change based on the design's bottleneck.

assertions.name: current_directive_identified
assertions.description: Current directive was identified from log
assertions.check: Output identifies the directive used (Default) from [Vivado_Tcl 4-137] or command line

assertions.name: diminishing_returns_diagnosed
assertions.description: Diminishing returns pattern was identified
assertions.check: Output notes the WNS improvement trend across passes and flags stagnation

assertions.name: specific_directive_recommended
assertions.description: A specific alternative directive was recommended
assertions.check: Output recommends a specific directive (AggressiveExplore, AggressiveFanoutOpt, etc.) with justification based on the design's bottleneck type

evals.name: srl-shift-register-opt
evals.prompt: I see shift register optimization messages in the phys_opt log. Were any SRLs decomposed for timing? Should I enable -shift_register_opt?
evals.expected_output: Agent extracts [Physopt 32-677/1123/1401/1402] SRL optimization messages, reports candidates vs results.

assertions.name: srl_messages_checked
assertions.description: SRL optimization messages were extracted
assertions.check: Output references [Physopt 32-677], [Physopt 32-1123], [Physopt 32-1401], or [Physopt 32-1402] shift register optimization messages

assertions.name: option_guidance
assertions.description: Guidance on -shift_register_opt option was provided
assertions.check: Output discusses whether -shift_register_opt should be enabled and potential trade-offs (area vs timing)

evals.name: slr-crossing-optimization
evals.prompt: My multi-die design has timing failures on SLR crossing paths. What did phys_opt_design do for SLR crossings?
evals.expected_output: Agent extracts [Physopt 32-1411/1492] SLR replication messages and [Physopt 32-949] DFX interface replication messages, reports SLR-specific optimizations.

assertions.name: slr_messages_checked
assertions.description: SLR crossing optimization messages were extracted
assertions.check: Output references [Physopt 32-1411] (SLR replication candidates) or [Physopt 32-1492] (SLR candidate net) or -slr_crossing_opt option

assertions.name: slr_recommendation
assertions.description: SLR-specific recommendation was provided
assertions.check: Output recommends -slr_crossing_opt, pipeline register insertion at SLR boundaries, or floorplan adjustments
